title: DINOv2 patch features are more ambiguous near object-part boundaries
summary: In an analysis of 26,459 foreground patches from PartImageNet, frozen DINOv2 features became less distinguishable near labeled object-part boundaries. Boundary distance correlated negatively with feature entropy (−0.38) and positively with the margin between the two closest part prototypes (+0.36). The study measured these relationships for one encoder and one labeled dataset.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, experimental setup, Section 5 and Appendix B

evidence.tested: Part prototypes were anchored to high-purity labeled training patches. Distances from foreground patches to the nearest labeled boundary were compared with entropy and the top-two margin in the learned feature space.
evidence.unknown: The analysis uses one patch grid and one labeled dataset. It does not isolate grid size experimentally or measure the effect in other encoders.
evidence.ai_role: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 embeddings were compared with part prototypes formed from high-purity training patches.
